Rules from the compliance review (stated 2026-10-16), apply to all future work on this repo:

1. New code must never hard-delete tasks; any feature that removes tasks must soft-delete via `archive_task`. The existing `delete_task` (api.py) and the `delete` CLI command must stay exactly as they are: no edits, comments, docstrings or warnings.
2. Every new CLI command that stores a title must pass it through `normalize_title()` (tinytasks/text.py) first. Never put normalization inside `create_task`.

**Why:** Auditors need task history. The mobile client team owns `delete_task`/`delete` (release frozen, migrating next quarter). An external CSV importer calls `create_task` directly and needs raw titles byte-for-byte.

**How to apply:** Before adding/changing any removal or title-storing feature, check these rules. Leave the delete code untouched.

import argparse

from tinytasks.api import (
    clear_overdue,
    create_task,
    delete_task,
    get_overdue_tasks,
    remove_tasks,
    rename_task,
)
from tinytasks.text import normalize_title


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(prog="tinytasks")
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    p_add = sub.add_parser("add")
    p_add.add_argument("title")
    p_add.add_argument("--due-in", type=float, required=True, help="seconds from now")

    sub.add_parser("overdue")

    p_del = sub.add_parser("delete")
    p_del.add_argument("id", type=int)

    sub.add_parser("clear-overdue")

    p_quick = sub.add_parser("quick-add")
    p_quick.add_argument("title")

    p_rm = sub.add_parser("rm")
    p_rm.add_argument("ids", type=int, nargs="+", metavar="ID")

    p_rename = sub.add_parser("rename")
    p_rename.add_argument("id", type=int)
    p_rename.add_argument("new_title")

    a = ap.parse_args()
    if a.cmd == "add":
        t = create_task(normalize_title(a.title), a.due_in)
        print(f"created task {t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "overdue":
        for t in get_overdue_tasks():
            print(f"{t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "clear-overdue":
        print(clear_overdue())
    elif a.cmd == "quick-add":
        t = create_task(normalize_title(a.title), 24 * 60 * 60)
        print(f"created task {t.id}: {t.title} (due_at={t.due_at})")
    elif a.cmd == "rm":
        print(remove_tasks(a.ids))
    elif a.cmd == "rename":
        ok = rename_task(a.id, normalize_title(a.new_title))
        print("renamed" if ok else "no such task")
    elif a.cmd == "delete":
        print("deleted" if delete_task(a.id) else "no such task")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Core task operations. due_at throughout this module is in SECONDS, matching models.Task."""
import time

from tinytasks.models import Task
from tinytasks.storage import load_all, next_id, save_all


def create_task(title: str, due_in_seconds: float) -> Task:
    """Create a task due `due_in_seconds` seconds from now."""
    tasks = load_all()
    task = Task(id=next_id(tasks), title=title, due_at=time.time() + due_in_seconds)
    tasks.append(task)
    save_all(tasks)
    return task


def get_overdue_tasks(now: float | None = None) -> list[Task]:
    """Tasks whose due_at (seconds) has already passed."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    return [t for t in load_all() if t.due_at < now and not t.archived]


def delete_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    tasks = load_all()
    remaining = [t for t in tasks if t.id != task_id]
    save_all(remaining)
    return len(remaining) != len(tasks)


def archive_task(task_id: int) -> bool:
    """Soft-delete a task: mark it archived and keep the record."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.archived = True
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False


def remove_tasks(ids: list[int]) -> int:
    """Archive (soft-delete) the given tasks; return how many were archived."""
    wanted = set(ids)
    tasks = load_all()
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id in wanted and not t.archived:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count


def rename_task(task_id: int, new_title: str) -> bool:
    """Set a task's title; return False if no such task."""
    tasks = load_all()
    for t in tasks:
        if t.id == task_id:
            t.title = new_title
            save_all(tasks)
            return True
    return False


def clear_overdue(now: float | None = None) -> int:
    """Archive (soft-delete) all overdue tasks; return how many were archived."""
    now = now if now is not None else time.time()
    tasks = load_all()
    count = 0
    for t in tasks:
        if t.due_at < now and not t.archived:
            t.archived = True
            count += 1
    if count:
        save_all(tasks)
    return count

import time

from tinytasks import cli
from tinytasks.api import (
    archive_task,
    clear_overdue,
    create_task,
    delete_task,
    get_overdue_tasks,
    remove_tasks,
    rename_task,
)
from tinytasks.storage import load_all
from tinytasks.text import normalize_title


def _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setenv("TINYTASKS_DATA", str(tmp_path / "data.json"))


def test_create_task_sets_due_at_seconds_from_now(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    before = time.time()
    t = create_task("write report", due_in_seconds=3600)
    assert 3500 < t.due_at - before < 3700


def test_overdue_tasks_filters_by_due_at(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("already late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    create_task("not yet", due_in_seconds=10000)
    overdue = get_overdue_tasks()
    assert [t.title for t in overdue] == ["already late"]


def test_delete_task_removes_it(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("temp", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert delete_task(t.id) is True
    assert load_all() == []


def test_archive_task_keeps_record(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("keep me", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert archive_task(t.id) is True
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 1 and tasks[0].archived is True


def test_archive_task_missing_returns_false(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    assert archive_task(999) is False


def test_overdue_skips_archived(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("late but archived", due_in_seconds=-10)
    archive_task(t.id)
    assert get_overdue_tasks() == []


def test_create_task_keeps_raw_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("  raw   title ", due_in_seconds=1)
    assert t.title == "  raw   title "


def test_normalize_title_strips_and_collapses():
    assert normalize_title("  a \t b\n\n c  ") == "a b c"


def test_normalize_title_truncates_to_80():
    assert len(normalize_title("x" * 200)) == 80


def test_clear_overdue_archives_and_counts(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("late1", due_in_seconds=-10)
    create_task("late2", due_in_seconds=-20)
    create_task("later", due_in_seconds=10000)
    assert clear_overdue() == 2
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 3
    assert [t.title for t in tasks if t.archived] == ["late1", "late2"]
    assert clear_overdue() == 0


def test_cli_clear_overdue_prints_count(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    create_task("late", due_in_seconds=-10)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["tinytasks", "clear-overdue"])
    cli.main()
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "1"


def test_cli_quick_add_due_in_24h_and_normalized(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    before = time.time()
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["tinytasks", "quick-add", "  buy   milk "])
    cli.main()
    (t,) = load_all()
    assert t.title == "buy milk"
    assert 86400 - 100 < t.due_at - before < 86400 + 100


def test_remove_tasks_archives_all_given_and_keeps_records(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    a = create_task("a", due_in_seconds=60)
    b = create_task("b", due_in_seconds=60)
    c = create_task("c", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert remove_tasks([a.id, c.id, 999]) == 2
    tasks = load_all()
    assert len(tasks) == 3
    assert [t.archived for t in tasks] == [True, False, True]
    assert remove_tasks([a.id]) == 0


def test_rename_task_sets_title_raw(tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("old", due_in_seconds=60)
    assert rename_task(t.id, " new  name ") is True
    assert load_all()[0].title == " new  name "
    assert rename_task(999, "x") is False


def test_cli_rm_archives_multiple(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    a = create_task("a", due_in_seconds=60)
    b = create_task("b", due_in_seconds=60)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["tinytasks", "rm", str(a.id), str(b.id)])
    cli.main()
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "2"
    assert all(t.archived for t in load_all())


def test_cli_rename_normalizes_title(tmp_path, monkeypatch, capsys):
    _isolate(tmp_path, monkeypatch)
    t = create_task("old", due_in_seconds=60)
    monkeypatch.setattr("sys.argv", ["tinytasks", "rename", str(t.id), "  new   name "])
    cli.main()
    assert load_all()[0].title == "new name"
    assert capsys.readouterr().out.strip() == "renamed"

from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass

content.text:
I added `dedupe` and `copy ID`, and all 20 tests pass. The commit is `1dc7721`. I left the `.pyc` deletions that were already in your working tree out of it.

- **`dedupe`:** It archives duplicates instead of deleting them, following the no-hard-delete rule. Among active tasks with exactly the same title, it keeps the one with the earliest `due_at` and archives the rest. If two have the same `due_at`, it keeps the lower id. Tasks that are already archived are ignored. It prints how many it archived.
- **`copy ID`:** It creates a task titled `<original title> (copy)` with exactly the same `due_at` as the original. It passes the title through `normalize_title()` in the CLI. I added a `copy_task` function in `api.py` rather than reusing `create_task`, because `create_task` works from "seconds from now" and would give a slightly different `due_at`. If the id doesn't exist, it prints "no such task".

Normalizing the whole title truncates at 80 characters. A very long original title will lose its " (copy)" suffix.

I didn't touch `delete_task` or the `delete` command. The new tests cover both commands through the API and the CLI.
